title: Open extension by zero and unbounded derived tensor on ordinary etale sites
statement:
Let $C$ be a commutative ring and $j:U\hookrightarrow T$ an open immersion of schemes [def-weil-open-immersion]. Work in the ordinary unbounded derived categories $D(U_{\mathrm{et}},C)$ and $D(T_{\mathrm{et}},C)$ of constant-ring module sheaves [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], with derived tensor [def-kun-derived-tensor]. Let $j_!$ be termwise extension by zero [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero] and $j^*$ termwise exact inverse image [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]. For every $K\in D(U_{\mathrm{et}},C)$ and $M\in D(T_{\mathrm{et}},C)$, the canonical open tensor comparison is a natural isomorphism
$$
(j_!K)\otimes_C^L M\xrightarrow{\sim}j_!(K\otimes_C^L j^*M).
$$
Here the canonical comparison is the derived comparison induced by the sheaf tensor identity $j_!P\otimes_C N\cong j_!(P\otimes_C j^*N)$ on the localized small etale site, with direct-sum total tensor on complexes. There is no boundedness, constructibility, Tor-amplitude, finiteness, or invertibility hypothesis on $C$, $K$, or $M$.

lean.note: Specialize A to ModuleCat.{u + 1} C, C : Type (u + 1), [CommRing C], and j : U ⟶ T with [IsOpenImmersion j]. Take the inverse of this natural isomorphism of bifunctors: its components go from (j_! K) tensor^L M to j_!(K tensor^L Lj^* M). Compose with j_! applied to tensoring K with leftDerivedUpperStarIsoMapDerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u + 1} C) j, giving exactly the node with termwise exact j^*. The displayed generic coefficient hypotheses are all instances for ModuleCat C; in particular upperStarPreservesFlat_moduleCat is supplied by WeilConjectures.SixFunctors.Etale.UpperLowerStar.FlatModuleCat. The scratch specialization was compiled with only CommRing C and IsOpenImmersion j as hypotheses. The isomorphism is asIso of the canonical projection mate of the exact derived adjunction, using the derived tensor comparison induced from ordinary sheaf tensor. Its inverse is the canonical comparison of Stacks 0GL1/0E8I. No boundedness, constructibility, Tor-amplitude, finiteness or invertibility condition is imposed. Uses the existing definitions recorded in all five statement dependencies; no second tensor or extension-by-zero construction.
